linkedin.text:
🚨 Your agent keeps using twenty words where one will do.

You drop Claude or Codex into a project, and it starts inventing its own jargon. "Materialization cascade" becomes "when a lesson inside a section of a course is made real and given a spot in the file system." Every. Single. Session.

Matt Pocock's **skills repo** (⭐ 208k) fixes this with one workflow: **slash grill-with-docs**.

It interviews you about the change you're making, then builds a **CONTEXT.md** file — a shared domain model that turns verbose explanations into concise, consistent language. The agent learns your project's ubiquitous language and stops overthinking.

✅ Variables, functions, and files stay consistently named
✅ The agent navigates your codebase faster because the language is tight
✅ You save tokens because the agent stops wasting them on verbose thinking

You also get **slash tdd** for red-green-refactor loops, **slash improve-codebase-architecture** for deepening surveys, and **slash ask-matt** to route you to the right workflow.

Install once on Claude Code or any agent. Two hundred thousand developers already use it daily.

**Search GitHub for "mattpocock/skills"** and install it in thirty seconds.

What's the most verbose thing your agent keeps saying? 👇
